name: genesis
description: A coding agent for endpoints that don't behave. mTLS, corporate CAs, token exchange, air-gapped.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Genesis executes what is in the open folder. An endpoint profile can name a transform module (arbitrary JavaScript, run before the first request) or an `exec` credential helper (a command, spawned to fetch a token), and .agent/mcp.json names programs to launch. None of that is safe to run from a repository you have not read, so Genesis stays off in Restricted Mode.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Genesis reads profiles, skills and agents from disk and confines the agent's writes to a real workspace folder, so it needs a filesystem rather than a virtual one.

genesis.instructionsFile.markdownDescription: Workspace-relative markdown file whose contents are prepended to every system prompt, for conventions that must hold on every turn. Absent is fine and is not warned about. Skills are the on-demand equivalent; this is the always-on one. Capped at 16,000 characters, with the truncation stated to the model.

genesis.microCompact.markdownDescription:
Condense old exchanges into a short summary instead of dropping them when the context window fills.

Without this, a long run silently loses its own beginning: the oldest turns are shifted off and replaced by a note telling the model to ask if it needs them, which it cannot - they are gone. With it, an exchange is summarised by a second, cheaper model and the summary stays in the conversation.

**Off by default, and that is a real trade rather than caution**. Absorbing an exchange rewrites the middle of the prompt, and the middle of the prompt is inside the cached prefix - so this buys window headroom by giving up prompt-cache hits. Worth it when the alternative is losing the turns; not worth it on a conversation that was never going to fill the window.

Name the summariser with `#genesis.microCompactProfile#`; it is never chosen for you, and it needs a context window of at least 64,000 tokens. Without one this stays off and says so in the log; nothing fails.

genesis.microCompactProfile.markdownDescription:
Which endpoint profile condenses old exchanges when `#genesis.microCompact#` is on. Name it by its `name:` field.

**Micro-compaction does not run until this is set**, and there is deliberately no automatic choice. Condensing means sending part of the conversation - including file contents and command output the agent read - to a second endpoint, and which endpoint that is should be a decision rather than a guess. Picking one automatically would quietly route a local-only workspace's code to whatever cloud profile happened to be configured beside it.

The profile needs a context window of at least 64,000 tokens; a smaller one is refused and the log says so. A cheap `kind: chat` model is the right choice: condensing is the least demanding thing a model can be asked to do, and pointing it at a reasoning profile spends a thinking budget on paraphrase.

genesis.microCompactEveryNTurns.markdownDescription: How often micro-compaction may absorb an exchange, in turns. At most one exchange is ever condensed per attempt. Raise it to rewrite the prompt less often, which costs less cache; lower it to reclaim room faster. Hermes's `micro_compact_every_n_turns`.

genesis.microCompactDefragThresholdToken.markdownDescription: How many reclaimable tokens have to be sitting in the compactable middle of a conversation before summarising one is worth a request. Below this, the summary call costs more than the room it wins back. Hermes's `micro_compact_defrag_threshold_tokens`.

genesis.editorContext.markdownDescription: Append what is on screen - the focused file, the open tabs, and the compiler's errors for that file - to each message you send. Costs a few hundred tokens per turn and is what makes "fix this" resolve to something. Turn it off on a very small context window.

genesis.readOutsideWorkspace.markdownDescription:
Let the agent **read** files outside the workspace folder - a Python `site-packages`, a Go module cache, a config under `/etc`. Without it, asking about a library your code imports gets "outside the workspace" and no answer, because the dependency source is never in the checkout.

**Writes are always confined to the workspace**, whatever this is set to, and paths whose whole purpose is holding a credential - `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, `.kube`, `id_rsa`, `.netrc` and similar - are refused even when this is on. Turn it off to confine reads to the workspace as well.

genesis.browserHeaded.markdownDescription: Show the browser the agent drives in a real window instead of running it headless. Off by default, because a window appearing over your editor every time the agent looks something up is worse than not seeing it - but turn it on when you want to watch what it is doing, or drive it yourself mid-task. Takes effect the next time the browser starts.

genesis.activeProfile.description: Name of the active endpoint profile. First valid profile is used when empty.

genesis.approvalMode.description: When tools run without confirming: ask = every side effect; edits-auto = file edits auto, shell commands ask; full-auto = never ask.

genesis.caBundlePath.markdownDescription:
Global fallback CA bundle merged into every profile's `tls.caBundle` at load time. Accepts a file path or the literal `system`.

Machine-scoped on purpose: this is an absolute path on **your** machine, so it must not be written into a repository's workspace settings, where it would resolve to nothing for everybody else who clones it.

genesis.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show the `Explain`, `Document` and `Tests` actions above functions and classes.

genesis.codeActions.description: Offer Genesis fixes and rewrites in the lightbulb menu.

genesis.inlineCompletion.markdownDescription: Suggest code at the cursor as ghost text. Off by default: this needs a fast fill-in-the-middle endpoint, which most corporate gateways are not. The active profile must also set `capabilities.fim: true`.

genesis.searchProvider.markdownDescription: Which service `web_search` queries. `duckduckgo` needs no key and is the default. The others need `#genesis.searchApiKey#`, and Google also needs `#genesis.searchEngineId#`. A provider named without its credential falls back to `duckduckgo` rather than failing.

genesis.searchApiKey.markdownDescription:
API key for the search provider.

**Point this at the key rather than pasting it**: `${env:BRAVE_KEY}` and `${file:~/.config/brave.key}` both work, the same as in an endpoint profile. A literal here is stored in the clear.

Machine-scoped, so it cannot be set in a repository's workspace settings and committed.

genesis.searchEngineId.markdownDescription: Google Programmable Search engine id (`cx`). Google only.

genesis.browserProfile.markdownDescription: `persistent` keeps the agent browser's cookies and history between launches, so a login it performs survives closing the window. `fresh` starts from an empty temp profile every time, which is the old behaviour. Neither affects bot detection.

scripts.test:package: npm run package && node test/run.js vsix render mentions activate-vsix --include-tagged
scripts.verify: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run test:package
